candidates.exact_span: 4Q3   Lowest four-day average flow rate expected to occur once every three-years
candidates.computation_change_reason: If 4Q3 is interpreted differently (statistical recurrence, averaging window, or which flow records qualify), flow-dependent effluent limits or flow-triggered monitoring conditions referenced elsewhere may be matched to the wrong discharge period or left unresolved.

Treating BMP as a numeric effluent limit versus a non-numeric management obligation (or as 'practices' rather than 'plan') changes whether Purpose A performs numeric exceedance comparisons and whether Purpose B treats the item as a monitoring/reporting requirement.

candidates.exact_span: BOD   Biochemical oxygen demand (five-day unless noted otherwise)
candidates.computation_change_reason: A different reading of whether the five-day test applies by default could pair reported measurements with the wrong BOD limit or monitoring parameter, changing exceedance findings and which BOD monitoring obligations are considered applicable.

If critical dilution is interpreted with a different mixing-zone or dilution-factor meaning, dilution-dependent numeric limits derived from receiving-water conditions may be applied at incorrect values.

Whether an obligation or result counts as a DMR (versus another report type) affects whether monitoring was required/performed for Purpose B and whether missing or non-numeric entries are treated as documented reporting gaps versus other no-data states in Purpose C.

candidates.exact_span: ug/L       Micrograms per litter (one part per billion)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The definition equates ug/L to parts per billion; an alternate reading of the unit (including the 'litter' wording) could mis-scale concentrations when comparing reported measurements to limits stated in ug/L or converted units.

How MQL is applied to reported values (especially non-detects or values below quantification) can change whether a numeric compliance comparison is attempted in Purpose A and whether Purpose C classifies the period as documented no-data, inadequate evidence, or unresolved.

Reasonable-potential determinations govern whether certain numeric limits are included or triggered; a different interpretation of RP could change which limits are treated as enforceable for comparison.
pH limits are expressed in standard units; misinterpreting s.u. or its scope could cause pH measurements to be compared against the wrong scale or parameter form.

Classifying a limit as a TBEL versus another limit type affects whether it is treated as an enforceable numeric discharge limit subject to exceedance analysis or as a different non-comparable requirement.
